provenance.note: Budgets are caps for build/export QA, not targets; measured audits of our own assets live in that document's section 7.

desktop_glb.label: Desktop GLB (AnthroForge app, Babylon; showcase renders)

webgl_mobile.label: WebGL / mobile — Telegram Mini App (phone webview, Babylon)
webgl_mobile.notes: Cutout core mandatory (FUR_BUDGETS.md section 6); KTX2/Basis required for textures; the page renders at half device resolution — keep that, it is worth more than any fur optimisation.

second_life.label: Second Life (Bento export profile)
second_life.halving_rule: each lower LOD may carry ~half the triangles of the one above with no download-weight penalty
second_life.lowest_rule: Lowest must be hand-authored (impostor-grade cross-quads or a slim silhouette shell)

rows.notes: silhouette-critical; longest fur earns the most tris
shell cost rides on the body LOD's zone tris, not a card count

rows.technique: texture + fresnel fuzz; shells x4 max on desktop

zones_lod0.density_note: production LOD0 ~4,700 placements vs the prototype's 1,700 (~2.8x) = ~1.28x body-surface quad ratio, the minimum at which a card coat stops reading as tufts on clay; ruff-heavy species push toward 1.5x

lod_switching.metric: screen-height fraction f = character height / viewport height

tiers.content: half card placements, shells x3, texture mip bias +1
quarter placements (silhouette zones only), shells off, body zones texture-only
texture-only fur; impostor cross-quads if the naked silhouette reads wrong

lod_switching.hysteresis: switch down at f, back up at f x 1.15; minimum dwell 0.5 s; bias one tier up within 10% of a boundary when the camera moves toward the character
lod_switching.per_zone: zone tier = global tier, +1 for ruff/tail, -1 for belly/bodyhair
lod_switching.textures: textures are NOT per-LOD; all geometry LODs share one texture set, resolution steps via mip bias
